title: ECB announces €750 billion Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme (PEPP)
attribution: European Central Bank; English summary by MacroPulse AI
text: At the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, the ECB Governing Council announced the temporary PEPP with an initial envelope of EUR 750 billion. The programme included purchases of public and private securities in response to risks to monetary policy transmission and the euro area economy. This policy announcement does not quantify an effect on GDP or the EUR/USD reference exchange rate.

title: Coordinated central bank action to enhance the provision of global US dollar liquidity
attribution: European Central Bank; English summary by MacroPulse AI
text: In March 2020, the ECB and other central banks announced coordinated swap-line action to provide US dollar liquidity. They reduced operation pricing and introduced an 84-day maturity. This measure concerns access to USD funding. Its date provides historical context for EUR/USD during the pandemic, without identifying a causal effect on reference exchange rates.

title: Our monetary policy statement at a glance — March 2022
attribution: European Central Bank; English summary by MacroPulse AI
text: In March 2022, the ECB described how the Russian invasion of Ukraine raised energy costs, disrupted trade and weakened confidence. It also observed increases in food and other goods and services. This was the ECB assessment of channels and expectations at that date. Observed inflation values are obtained separately from HICP.

title: Annual inflation up to 10.6% in the euro area
attribution: European Commission, Eurostat; MacroPulse AI summary, for which Eurostat is not responsible
text: Eurostat reported annual headline euro area HICP inflation of 10.6% in October 2022, following 9.9% in September. Energy made the largest contribution among the main components in this release. The figures concern the euro area and the November publication vintage, distinguishing percentage-point contributions from percentage annual inflation.

title: ECB monetary policy decisions of 21 July 2022
attribution: European Central Bank; English summary by MacroPulse AI
text: The ECB Governing Council announced a 50 basis point increase in its three policy rates on 21 July 2022. The deposit facility rate became 0.00% effective 27 July. The decision date differs from the effective date represented by the DFR series.

title: ECB monetary policy decisions of 14 September 2023

text: In September 2023, the ECB announced a 25 basis point increase in its policy rates. It set the deposit facility rate at 4.00% per year effective 20 September. The announced increase and the annual rate level have different units.
